entry.title: Course plans step 5: MCP tools and plan-aware snapshot
entry.content:
Course plans step 5: MCP tools and plan-aware snapshot

External assistants (Claude Desktop, Codex, any MCP client) can now do the
same job as the in-app planner. propose_course_plan writes a course-plan
packet — ordered units, 1-3 item types, optional proposed items per unit, and
the source material — and propose_items drops drafts into an existing course's
review queue, optionally targeting a unit. Both land in the Inbox and never
bypass the human gate; add_items/create_course keep their import-as-is
behaviour and now point at the review-queue tools for drafted content.

snapshot.json exposes each course's plan (units, what's open, dates, pending
proposals per unit), the current level, item levels, and a pending-proposals
count, so an assistant can see the syllabus structure before proposing.
list_courses prints the plan summary. 218 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Course plans step 4: plan page, review queue UI, entry points
entry.content:
Course plans step 4: plan page, review queue UI, entry points

Dashboard gains "From my material": paste a syllabus or notes, pick how units
release (by progress, by date, by hand), get an editable outline back — course
name, item types, units with item targets and dates — and create the course
with nothing in it yet. The new /plan/:courseId page is where the work
happens: one card per unit showing released/current/locked state, dates in
schedule mode, item and pass counts, a draft button with count and steer, and
the review queue with pending/rejected/accepted tabs. Rows show fields,
alternates, mnemonic, handle and prerequisites, a validation error or a
duplicate flag; accept, edit in a modal (fields, alternates, note, handle,
prerequisites), reject with an optional reason, restore, forget; accept-all and
reject-all per unit; release-mode switch and "Release next unit"; add a unit.

The Course page links to the plan and shows the current unit; the Dashboard
badges pending proposals; scheduled releases catch up at boot and whenever the
plan page opens. Verified in the browser against a pasted plan packet.

entry.title: Course plans step 3: two-stage AI pipeline
entry.content:
Course plans step 3: two-stage AI pipeline

ai/plan.ts reads the learner's own material in two stages. planCourse returns
an OUTLINE for review — ordered units with topics, target counts, and any
dates the material gives, plus 1-3 item types (typed or multiple-choice
templates) — and writes nothing. generateUnitItems drafts items for ONE unit
on demand into the review queue, sending what is already in the course (with
keys usable as prerequisites) and what the learner rejected (with reasons) so
the model avoids both. A rerun costs one unit, not the course.

The material rides as a second system block: on Anthropic it carries a cache
breakpoint so consecutive unit calls pay a fraction for it; on
OpenAI-compatible endpoints it is appended. Material past 150k characters is
cut with a visible flag, never silently. outlineProblems catches dangling
field references before a course is created. The model is mocked in tests;
216 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Course plans step 2: review-queue verbs and release modes
entry.content:
Course plans step 2: review-queue verbs and release modes

services/proposals.ts is the human gate: accept turns pending proposals into
real items at their unit's level (locked until the unit is released, otherwise
straight into the lesson queue), resolving prerequisite handles to accepted
items across batches and in any order within one; a handle that points at a
still-pending row holds the item with a message, a rejected one is dropped
with a warning, and a row that fails validation is skipped with the error
written onto it rather than thrown. Reject with a reason, restore, edit before
accepting, accept-all-valid per unit, and a recheck after type edits.

services/plans.ts owns release: manual (release next unit), schedule (the
level floor follows unit dates, never backwards), and progress (hands the
level to the existing engine). Plus unit edits, appending a unit, a per-unit
progress read for the plan page, and the in-app createPlannedCourse that
routes through the same packet path as MCP. 206 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Course plans step 1: storage, packet kinds, autoAdvance
entry.content:
Course plans step 1: storage, packet kinds, autoAdvance

Progressive AI courses need a place for a syllabus and a human gate in front
of the AI. Two additive Dexie v3 tables: plans (units that map 1:1 onto course
levels, release mode, source material) and proposals (the review queue —
pending/accepted/rejected items carrying validation errors and duplicate
flags, so a generation is never lost by closing a panel).

The packet format gains two kinds: course-plan (course + types + ordered
units; unit items land in the review queue, not the course) and propose-items
(items into an existing course's queue). Level config gains autoAdvance so a
plan in manual or scheduled release mode can hold the level while
prerequisite unlocks keep working. Backups round-trip both tables; deleting a
course removes them; the Inbox summarizes the new kinds. 190 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Multiple choice reviews
entry.content:
Multiple choice reviews

Any template can now be answered by clicking an option (or pressing 1-6)
instead of typing. Wrong options come from the same question asked of sibling
items, preferring items within one level so the odd one out isn't a giveaway.

Every candidate distractor is run through the real grading pipeline first and
kept only if it grades incorrect — so an accepted synonym, something inside the
typo budget, or a guidance answer can never be offered as a wrong option.
Choosing an option submits its text down the same path a typed answer takes,
so grading, ghosts, gating and the SRS commit are identical.

Templates with too few siblings fall back to the typed box rather than showing
a giveaway. Packets (and the MCP create_course tool) can declare mode "choice"
with an option count.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Phase 3: content-model UI, media, manual SRS control
entry.content:
Phase 3: content-model UI, media, manual SRS control

Item-type designer: fields (text/rich text/list/image/audio/cloze) with kinds
and reordering, a template editor (prompt/answer/hints, typed vs sentence-cloze,
kana IME, typo tolerance), live validation, and an impact preview. Saving
migrates every item of the type in one transaction: new templates create cards
and send the item back to lessons, removed templates delete their cards and
history, removed or retyped fields convert their values.

Item editor: field values, rich-text mnemonics, prerequisites (cycle-guarded),
per-template synonyms / block lists / guidance answers, and manual SRS control
(set stage, reset, suspend, resume, burn) written as kind:"manual" logs with
the previous snapshot and undoable as a group.

Media: images downscaled to 1024px and re-encoded to WebP on ingest, rendered
in lessons and reviews, carried through JSON backups as base64, and swept when
nothing references them.

Also: Alt+H progressive hints, an empty-prompt guard, and lesson/active status
healing in recomputeUnlocks. 166 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Phase 2: prerequisite gating, levels, kana IME, Japanese course
entry.content:
Phase 2: prerequisite gating, levels, kana IME, Japanese course

- engine/gating.ts + engine/levels.ts: pure unlock/level math (chains,
  diamonds, sticky passes, cycle guard, level thresholds)
- services/gating.ts: applyGatingAfterReview runs inside commitReview's
  transaction (item passes -> unlock dependents -> cascade level-ups);
  recomputeUnlocks repairs graphs and re-evaluates levels; one-time
  backfill derives passedAt for pre-Phase-2 courses
- items/packets/seeds carry level + prereqs; packets use local keys with
  an earlier-definition rule (also guarantees acyclicity); export is
  topologically sorted and never emits out-of-packet edges
- Japanese seed: radical -> kanji -> vocab across two levels, kanji as
  the level gate, kana-typed reading cards
- wanakana kana IME in the answer box (moku -> もく), katakana answers
  accept hiragana, kanji blanks never switch to kana mode
- CoursePage Progress panel (level bar, lock tallies, stage distribution,
  Recheck unlocks), lock badges with reasons, prereq/level pickers,
  level-mode settings; session summary shows unlocks and level-ups
- 15 adversarial-review fixes: flat courses no longer enforce a level
  gate, deleteItem scrubs dangling prereq edges, recompute re-evaluates
  level-ups, IME preserves the caret, seeds fail loudly
- 120 tests passing

entry.title: Feature batch: multi-provider AI, ghosts, sentence-cloze, cram, stats…
entry.content:
Feature batch: multi-provider AI, ghosts, sentence-cloze, cram, stats, capture, Anki import, TTS

- AI providers: Anthropic or any OpenAI-compatible API (OpenAI, Gemini,
  OpenRouter, keyless Ollama) with JSON-mode fallback + zod validation
- Ghost reviews (Bunpro-style): policy-gated drill copies on a short
  ladder; graduation deletes, undo resurrects from the log
- Sentence-cloze: rotating example sentences with masked blanks, cloze
  seed course, editor + packet + export/import support
- Cram/extra study (learned / leeches / missed-this-week), zero SRS effect
- Stats: DST-safe review heatmap, true all-time retention, per-course bars
- Quick capture inbox (Dexie v2) with convert-to-item flow
- Anki .apkg import (legacy schema) with field mapping + kana detection
- Browser TTS on cards and lessons (user-initiated, unmount-cancelled)
- AI leech rescue in the session summary
- 21 adversarial-review fixes incl. cloze export kind, degenerate blanks,
  ghost/ladder-edit isolation, commit-failure surfacing
- 89 tests passing
